channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Criminal – Sentencing – Mitigating role
item.description: Where a defendant has challenged the denial of a three-level role reduction in her sentencing range, the sentencing court failed to perform the correct mitigating role analysis, so a remand for resentencing must be ordered.

item.title: Immigration – Persecution – Nexus
item.description: Where a petitioner’s applications for asylum and withholding of removal were denied, that decision should be upheld because the petitioner (1) has shown neither past persecution nor a nexus to her claimed particular social groups and (2) has not established that the Honduran government would be unwilling or unable to protect her from private actors.

item.title: Boston lawyers secure $209K verdict for victim of email scam
item.description: A federal judge awarded nearly $209K to a businessman whose wire transfer was diverted in an email hacking scam, finding a Massachusetts intermediary liable for conversion.

item.title: Whistleblower: Ex-DOGE member took Social Security data to new job
item.description: A former DOGE software engineer is accused of transferring sensitive Social Security data to a private employer, prompting an SSA Inspector General investigation.

item.title: Healey taps attorney, assistant clerk-magistrate for judgeships
item.description: Gov. Maura Healey on March 11 nominated a longtime sole practitioner to the Boston Municipal Court bench and a Somerville District Court assistant clerk-magistrate to become a judge on the Juvenile Court.

item.title: Reciprocal court-ordered psychological exam upheld by SJC
item.description: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court ruled that defendants who use expert psychological exams in resentencing can be court-ordered to undergo reciprocal psychiatric evaluations.

item.title: Costco customers sue for share of refunds from Trump tariffs
item.description: Costco is sued in a US nationwide class action seeking refunds for higher prices due to Trump-imposed tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court.

item.title: Student erroneously told skin lesion malignant melanoma
item.description: The plaintiff had a lesion removed from her clavicle following a routine skin check. The specimen was removed by defendant A and sent to defendant B for pathological analysis.

item.title: Boston College clinic aids pro se litigants in federal court
item.description: Boston College Law School launches a federal court clinic helping pro se litigants draft complaints, oppose motions and resolve civil cases in Massachusetts.

item.title: Recalibrating AI patent strategy: What the USPTO shift means — and what it doesn’t
item.description: Under new leadership, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office recently adjusted its approach to patentability of artificial intelligence technologies in multiple meaningful respects.
